name: Aldesleukin
route_note: High-dose IV bolus every 8 hours in hospital (licensed); low-dose SC regimens in some regions
owner: Iovance Biotherapeutics (Proleukin); Clinigen in some markets

discovery.by: Doris Morgan, Francis Ruscetti and Robert Gallo (US National Cancer Institute)
discovery.note: Described T-cell growth factor, later named interleukin-2; aldesleukin is a non-glycosylated E. coli-produced analogue.

tagline: Recombinant interleukin-2: early cancer immunotherapy for kidney cancer and melanoma
summary: Aldesleukin is a recombinant form of interleukin-2, a cytokine that drives T-cell and NK-cell proliferation. High-dose IL-2 produces durable complete remissions in a small fraction of patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma or melanoma, at the cost of severe capillary leak toxicity.
mechanism: Aldesleukin binds the IL-2 receptor complex (α, β and common γ chains) on T cells and NK cells, activating JAK1/JAK3–STAT5 signalling and stimulating proliferation, cytotoxicity and cytokine production.

At high doses it expands tumour-reactive effector cells, but it also stimulates regulatory T cells and causes a systemic inflammatory response with vascular leak. It is used to support the expansion of infused tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes after lifileucel therapy.

history.title: T-cell growth factor
history.detail: Morgan, Ruscetti and Gallo describe a factor that sustains T-cell growth in culture.

history.title: Gene cloned
history.detail: Taniguchi and colleagues clone the human IL-2 gene.

history.title: Rosenberg's first responses
history.detail: Rosenberg and colleagues at the NCI report regressions with high-dose IL-2 and LAK cells.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved for metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

history.title: Iovance acquisition
history.detail: Iovance Biotherapeutics acquires Proleukin from Clinigen.

history.title: TIL therapy
history.detail: FDA approves lifileucel (Amtagvi), a tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy given with aldesleukin.

pk.metabolism: Proteolysis, mainly in renal tubular cells

safety.boxed_warning: Restrict to patients with normal cardiac and pulmonary function; capillary leak syndrome; impaired neutrophil function with increased infection risk; withhold for moderate to severe lethargy or somnolence.

facts: High-dose IL-2 must be given in hospital, usually in an intensive care setting.
Complete responses are seen in roughly 5–10% of patients and are often very durable.
